$comment: The full-request template (four jobs: lint, unit-style test, sharded e2e, burn-in) written for the backend service that asked for one job and nothing else. This is the case negativeControls' 'no-element-the-request-did-not-ask-for' exists to catch, and it is a shape step-02's own template produces when adaptation is skipped.

The five requested elements are unaffected, because a superset of them is still present: the pull_request trigger, contents:read, the Node version, npm ci and npm test all appear somewhere in the four-job pipeline. Nine elements the request never named are counted: the push trigger, the schedule trigger, the npm run test:e2e invocation, the lint gate, the shard matrix, the burn-in job, and the artifact uploads in both the e2e and burn-in jobs (each upload step names both playwright-report/ and test-results/ in one path list, so it is counted once per job rather than once per path). mustNotEmit's seven tokens (schedule:, push:, workflow_dispatch, upload-artifact, burn-in, shard, npm run lint) each resolve against this document for the contract's own oracle, which is the corpus's second, independent statement of the same finding.
